newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks hold gains at midday.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks hold gains at midday.

text.p: The Dow Industrials were comfortably higher at midday as individual stocks drove the market in the absence of strong volume or new economic data.

Intel Corp was up on expectations of a strong earnings report after the closing bell. Caterpillar boosted the Dow after analysts said they believed third quarter earnings per share would rise 30 percent.
Oil stocks also were strong.
The Dow Industrials were up 46 points at 6015. Advances led declines 9 to 8 on volume of about 219 million shares.
Many investors stayed away as the bond market was closed for the U.S. Columbus Day holiday.

"In a thin market it is not hard to move prices higher or lower," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities. "This is the fourth time we have gotten over 6000 on the Dow, and I suspect that before the day is over we will find ourselves below.
"The 6000 level becomes less and less dramatic every time we cross it."
The day was dominated by earnings reports and forecasts.
Intel was up 3/4 to 106-1/8 and topped the Nasdaq most active list.
"How much are we going to pay for a positive surprise in this stock?" asked Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co. "Those earnings better be very, very good."

According to First Call, analysts expect Intel to report earnings per share of $1.25, up from $1.02 a year earlier. But analysts say unofficial "whisper" estimates are even higher and represent the target Intel must hit in order to really satisfy Wall Street.

Dow component Caterpillar was up 1-1/8 at 74-3/8. Analysts said Caterpillar, the world's largest construction and mining equipment maker, is expected to post a third quarter earnings per share increase of about 30 percent on Tuesday, with North American demand helping the gains.

Texaco Inc led energy stocks higher as oil prices surged, cresting to a new post-Gulf War high in London this morning. Crude prices rose in the U.S. on renewed fighting in Iraqi Kurdistan, which caught oil shares just as they were staging a technical break higher.
Texaco was up 3-1/8 at 101-1/4.
Exxon Corp was up 1-1/4 at 87-5/8, Chevron Corp was up 3/4 at 66-1/2, and Mobil Corp rose 1-3/4 to 118-7/8.

Such strength in the oil sector is a double-edged sword, Metz said. "It's not bullish for the overall market. It could signal commodity inflation, an involuntary tax on the consumer and increased corporate expenses," he said. "It's not ideal leadership."
The Dow Transportation Index, which often goes in the opposite direction from the price of crude, was down 12 points at 2064, with airlines suffering.
UAL Corp was down 1-1/8 at 44-1/4, AMR Corp was down 1-5/8 at 83-3/4, and Delta Air Lines Inc fell 1/2 to 69-3/8.
Analysts said investors were eagerly awaiting the September Consumer Price Index, due Wednesday. The index is expected to rise 0.3 percent, both overall and excluding food and energy.
-- Andrej Gustincic, Wall Street Desk 212-859-1737
